name: silvie-slime-sovereign-levelup-next-slime-discount-counters
notes: Silvie, Slime Sovereign (mdwbkuhtjm, CHAMPION, level 3): "Silvie Lineage. On Enter: The next Slime ally card you activate this turn costs 2 less to activate and enters the field with two additional buff counters on it. Ignore the elemental requirements of advanced element Slime cards you activate." Her On Enter clause (enterAbilities['mdwbkuhtjm:0'], GeneratedCode/GeneratedMacroCode.php) just calls AddGlobalEffects($player, 'mdwbkuhtjm'); two SEPARATE consumers then read that flag: activationCostModifierAbilities['mdwbkuhtjm:0'] applies a one-time -2 reserve-cost delta to the next Slime ally activated, and Custom/GameLogic.php's HandAddToField() (ALLY/TOKEN+SLIME-subtype branch) adds 2 extra buff counters and calls RemoveGlobalEffect() to consume the flag, the first time ANY Slime ally enters the controller's field afterward. She is level 3, one level above a level-2 champion, so rather than grinding out two real prior level-ups, the starting champion's CardID is patched directly to Silvie, With the Pack (nllCALIXDT, level 2, TAMER) -- CanChampionLevelUpIntoCard only checks the CURRENT champion's own printed CardLevel, not lineage (same technique as lorraine-arclight-saber-levelup) -- then a REAL level-up is performed at the start of player 1's second turn (myMaterial-0, confirmed live to be the correct, sole eligible choice among the MZMAYCHOOSE's 3 offered material-phase options). GOTCHA found and fixed while authoring this fixture: directly overwriting CardID via patchMzId does NOT populate Subcards the way a genuine level-up would (DoMaterialize pushes the outgoing champion onto Subcards itself) -- so patching only CardID left Subcards empty, erasing the FIRE lineage a real Spirit-of-Fire-rooted Silvie, With the Pack would carry, and Red Slime (FIRE) was rejected live with flash message 'Element not enabled: FIRE'. Fixed by also patching Subcards to ['LMyKyVC2O9'] (Spirit of Fire) at setup, alongside the CardID patch -- confirmed live this resolves the element check. Her 3-memory level-up cost is paid from 3 filler memory-zone cards (which end up in the graveyard, confirmed live, not memory -- Grand Archive's level-up memory cost is paid by discarding, same as other champion-level-up fixtures in this suite). Red Slime (mttsvbgl6f, printed reserve cost 3) is seeded to a known hand slot and played for real via FSM immediately after the level-up, in the same turn: confirmed live, only ONE reserve-payment click (not the printed 3) is needed to finish playing it, proving the cost actually dropped to 1, and it ends up on the field (p1Field-1) with Counters {"buff":2} it has no other way to acquire, proving the "enters with two additional buff counters" clause. Break/restore verified: temporarily short-circuiting the activationCostModifierAbilities['mdwbkuhtjm:0'] closure to `return 0;` made the fixture's own zone_count(myHand)==7 assertion fail (the single myHand-0 click no longer fully paid the still-3 reserve cost, leaving the materialize mid-payment and the decision queue non-empty at step 5); restoring the closure made it pass again. Full suite re-run clean after restoring. The separate "ignore the elemental requirements of advanced element Slime cards" static clause is a computed-effect clause with no stored flag to assert and is out of scope here.

rulesClauses: On Enter: The next Slime ally card you activate this turn costs 2 less to activate and enters the field with two additional buff counters on it.
